subject: Acme security: annotated Private/Dedicated network diagrams & CAIQ mapping
messages:
From: Paul Hudson <paul.hudson@acme-corp.com>
To: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Acme: request for annotated diagrams + CAIQ/SIG mapping

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. Acme's audit team has a round of follow-ups from our SOC 2 review and requested more granular evidence for Redwood's Private and Dedicated deployment isolation. In particular they asked for:

- Annotated network diagrams for Private and Dedicated (control plane vs data plane clearly labeled; per-tenant egress fences).
- A simple mapping table linking CAIQ/SIG questions to the specific artifact or diagram and page/anchor.
- A per-deployment list of egress translation (NAT) and egress destinations used by managed services.
- Clarification on KMS/HSM boundary and whether customer keys are stored or proxied in the private control plane.

The auditor asked to receive redacted versions by 2026-11-28 to keep the engagement on schedule. If you have a short pack (PDF or ZIP) that would be ideal; otherwise even a Drive folder with permissive access is fine.

Could you also confirm whether you can provide an SVG or Visio for the main topology? They prefer vector for their doc ingestion.

Appreciate it — happy to set a 30-min call if useful.

Paul
Security Engineering
Acme Corp
From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Hudson <paul.hudson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme: request for annotated diagrams + CAIQ/SIG mapping

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. We can assemble a redacted deliverable that covers Private and Dedicated topologies, plus a CAIQ->artifact crosswalk. A few quick clarifying points so we scope exactly what you need:

1) Do you need per-tenant logical diagrams (showing tenant identifiers and ACLs), or is a single per-deployment diagram with a per-tenant table sufficient?
2) For egress destinations — is a list of CIDRs/services acceptable, or do you need packet captures/flow logs?
3) KMS: we can show the boundary and the KMS integration pattern; if you need key provenance logs we may need an additional request and approval.

We will prepare: SVG topology, a CSV egress translation table, and a CAIQ mapping doc (PDF). Kimberly and Marcus — marking you both to prepare the artifacts. We aim to have a first pass by COB 2026-11-24 so Jordan can review and send the redacted bundle to Acme.

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Mon) 11:00am PT to triage.

— Jordan

Subject: Fwd: Acme request — inventory + annotated diagrams (deadline 11/28)

Forwarding Acme's ask — see attached raw questionnaire for context.

Ask list for the deliverable (please attach/produce these files into the shared Drive folder):
- private-dedicated-annotated-topology_v1.svg (vector: show control plane, data plane, tenant fences, peering, public egress path)
- egress-translation-table.csv (columns: service, source-cidr, translated-ip, destination, purpose)
- controlplane-segmentation-notes.md (short notes on partitioning, service accounts, and KMS boundaries)
- CAIQ-mapping.pdf (table mapping CAIQ/SIG question to artifact and anchor)

Redactions: replace internal service hostnames with stable service IDs (e.g., service-001). Remove any on-prem provider hostnames. Provide a minimal legend that explains redactions.

Deadline: 2026-11-24 COB for internal review. Tony in Audit wants the redacted ZIP to go out to Acme by 2026-11-24 so they get time to prep.

Att: acme-request-raw-questions.pdf

— Jordan
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme request — inventory + annotated diagrams (deadline 11/24)

Thanks — attaching an initial pass. Notes below and inline comments in the SVG:

Attachments: private-dedicated-annotated-topology_v1.svg; egress-translation-table.csv; controlplane-segmentation-notes.md

High-level notes:
- The SVG is vector and labeled for both Private (VPC-based customer-managed control plane) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with isolated VLANs). Control plane components are shaded blue, data plane shaded green. Each tenant is represented as a numbered tenant capsule; per-tenant ACLs are in the adjacent table (see sheet 2 in the Drive).
- Egress table: we included managed-service NAT addresses and canonical destination domains. We redacted internal monitoring endpoints and replaced them with MON-SERVICE-ID placeholders.
- KMS boundary: per our standard Private offering, customer key material remains in customer-managed KMS when configured; otherwise we act as a KMS proxy with envelope keys — see controlplane-segmentation-notes.md paragraph 2.

Open items I want you to confirm before we send:
1) Are we comfortable sharing the per-tenant ACL table? I stripped tenant names but it's still fairly granular.
2) Do we want to include the short runbook for emergency key rotation? Right now it's internal.

If you give the go-ahead I'll bundle into a ZIP and upload to the Drive link below.

— Kimberly
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference
